native_metadata_exact.title: A relation-incidence proof of Tohăneanu's low-exponent supersolvability conjecture
native_metadata_exact.description: Every finite central free hyperplane arrangement over a characteristic-zero field whose nonzero exponents are 1 or 2 with at most one 3 is supersolvable. This research note proves the full conjecture in Tohăneanu's Oberwolfach contribution using linear-relation formality, rank-two counts, a forced K4 incidence core and modular terminal-pencil extensions. The paper credits the earlier all-2, tree, rank-three and modular-pruning results and acknowledges Ferudun's matching October 12, 2026 preprint. The verification archive preserves the October 4 PR candidate and dated disclosure records, source/priority audits and reproducible exact computational diagnostics. No exhaustive first-priority or independent-development claim is made. AI tools were used extensively in solving, writing and verifying the work. This is an unrefereed preprint; internal AI reviews do not constitute independent human peer review.

raw_original_abstract_TeX: We prove that every finite central free arrangement over a field of characteristic zero whose nonzero exponents are $1$ or $2$, with at most one $3$, is supersolvable. Factorization and linear-relation formality restrict the incidence graph of the multiple rank-two flats to a tree or a subdivision of $K_4$ with trees attached. A direct modular-coatom argument then gives a maximal modular chain in every rank. This proves the full conjecture stated in Toh\u{a}neanu's Oberwolfach contribution. We credit the earlier all-$2$, tree, rank-three and modular-pruning results and acknowledge Ferudun's later matching full-target preprint. The accompanying package preserves the dated candidate, source audit and exact computational diagnostics. AI tools were used extensively in developing, writing and checking this work. This preprint is unrefereed; its internal AI reviews are not human peer review.
